definitions.explanation: A river or stream that flows into a larger river rather than directly into the sea. Also used figuratively for offshoots or secondary branches of movements or schools of thought.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{川|かわ}→川：02186_kawa⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{利根川|とねがわ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{支流|しりゅう}だ。
examples.english: This river is a tributary of the Tone River.

examples.japanese: {支流|しりゅう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{合流|ごうりゅう}→合流：11902_gouryuu⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{川|かわ}→川：02186_kawa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The tributaries merge and become a large river.

examples.japanese: {多摩川|たまがわ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧いくつ⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{支流|しりゅう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あり→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦それぞれ→それぞれ：01453_sorezore⟧⟦{独自|どくじ}→独自：05614_dokuji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{生態系|せいたいけい}→生態系：04626_seitaikei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っている→持つ：00478_motsu⟧。
examples.english: The Tama River has numerous tributaries, each with its own unique ecosystem.

notes:
Combines {支|し} (branch/support) and {流|りゅう} (flow/stream). The {支|し} character indicates something secondary or branching off from the main, as in ⟦{支店|してん}→支店：03185_shiten⟧ (branch office) or ⟦{支線|しせん}→支線：24370_shisen⟧ (branch line).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {支流|しりゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{分|わ}かれる→分かれる：10976_wakareru⟧: branch off into tributaries
- {支流|しりゅう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{合流|ごうりゅう}→合流：11902_gouryuu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: tributaries converge
- ⟦{最大|さいだい}→最大：04827_saidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{支流|しりゅう}: the largest tributary
- {支流|しりゅう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧さかのぼる: go upstream along a tributary

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{本流|ほんりゅう}→本流：25798_honryuu⟧: main stream, main current — the primary river into which tributaries flow; also used figuratively for the mainstream of a movement
- ⟦{源流|げんりゅう}→源流：13359_genryuu⟧: headwaters, source — the origin point of a river; figuratively, the origin of something
- ⟦{合流|ごうりゅう}→合流：11902_gouryuu⟧: confluence, merging — the point where rivers join together
